ici.definition: Inter-Chip Interconnect — the high-bandwidth links wiring TPU chips into a slice's torus — 3D on v4/v5p (six links per v5p chip, ~4,800 Gbps), 2D on v5e/v6e.

dcn.definition: Data Center Network — the (slower than ICI) network that carries traffic between TPU slices/pods in a Multislice job.

3d torus.definition: A 3D grid of chips whose edges wrap around, so there are no ends and any two chips stay a short hop apart.

slice.definition: A contiguous sub-volume of a TPU pod, wired into its own torus (3D on v4/v5p); you pick its shape to match your parallelism.

multislice.definition: Joining multiple slices/pods over the DCN for jobs bigger than one pod — cross-slice traffic is far slower than ICI.

data parallelism.definition: Each device holds a full copy of the model; gradients are all-reduced across devices every step. Rides a torus ring well. (DP)

tensor parallelism.definition: A single matmul is split across a group of devices. Bandwidth-hungry, so it's kept on the tightest, highest-bandwidth ICI axis. (TP)

pipeline parallelism.definition: The model's layers are split into stages on different devices; micro-batches stream through so every stage stays busy. (PP)
